narration.text: Why 1 landslide uncorked Mount St. Helens sideways.
Its whole north face slid away on May 18, 1980.
An earthquake set off the largest landslide in recorded history.
The collapse uncorked the volcano sideways, not upward.
The ash column rose 24 kilometres high.
So the most dangerous eruptions don't always go straight up.
